title: Injective projective-module maps over a nil local ring are pure
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring (a commutative ring with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) such that every element of $\mathfrak m$ is nilpotent. Let $P,Q$ be projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], without any finite-generation assumption, and let $u:P\to Q$ be an injective $A$-linear map. Then $u$ is universally injective: for every $A$-module $T$, the map $1_T\otimes u:T\otimes_A P\to T\otimes_A Q$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. In particular $u\otimes_A A/\mathfrak m$ is injective.

source.place: Tags 05GM (definition-auto-ass), 05GN (lemma-auto-ass-implies-P), and 05GQ (lemma-P-fPD-zero), implication (1) to (2); specialization to a local ring with nil maximal ideal.

proof.text: The maximal ideal is proper, so $A\ne0$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-over-local-free] separately to $P$ and $Q$: its statement permits arbitrary projective modules over a commutative local ring, so choose bases $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of $P$ and $(q_b)_{b\in B}$ of $Q$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. We will prove by induction that every injection from a finite free module into any free $A$-module has an $A$-linear retraction, and then apply this to finite subsets of the basis of $P$. No global retraction for $u$ will be needed.

source.place: Tag 0593, theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring; the free-module reduction at the beginning of Tag 05GP, lemma-P-universally-injective

proof.text: For any finite list $a_1,\ldots,a_s\in\mathfrak m$, there is a nonzero $y\in A$ with $ya_j=0$ for every $j$. Indeed, choose $d_j\ge1$ with $a_j^{d_j}=0$ and put $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_s)$. For $D=1+\sum_j(d_j-1)$ every product of $D$ generators contains $a_j^{d_j}$ for some $j$, so $J^D=0$. Let $r\ge1$ be least with $J^r=0$ and choose $0\ne y\in J^{r-1}$; this is possible because $J^0=A\ne0$. Then $yJ=0$. For the empty list, take $y=1$. This proves directly the specialization of property (P) used in the source, without assuming that $\mathfrak m$ itself is nilpotent.

source.place: Tag 05GN, lemma-auto-ass-implies-P, property (P), specialized to finitely many nilpotent elements; elementary expansion of powers of the finitely generated ideal

proof.text: Set up the induction simultaneously for every free target $F$: if $v:A^n\to F$ is injective, construct $r_v:F\to A^n$ with $r_vv=1$. For $n=0$ use the zero map. Let $n\ge1$ and assume the assertion for $n-1$ and all free targets. Choose a basis $(q_b)_{b\in B}$ of $F$ and write the finite basis expansion $v(e_1)=\sum_b a_bq_b$ using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. If all its coefficients lay in $\mathfrak m$, step 2 would give $y\ne0$ killing them all; then $v(ye_1)=0$ contradicts injectivity. Thus some coefficient $a=a_{b_0}$ is outside $\mathfrak m$ and hence is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]. Define $\lambda:F\to A$ by $\lambda(\sum_bx_bq_b)=a^{-1}x_{b_0}$. It is $A$-linear and $\lambda(v(e_1))=1$.

source.place: Tag 05GP, lemma-P-universally-injective, induction on the rank of the source and splitting of its first basis vector; local specialization using Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring

proof.text: Continue this induction step. Put $H=\ker\lambda$ and $\pi(x)=x-v(e_1)\lambda(x)$. The equality $\lambda\pi=0$ and the identity $\pi|_H=1_H$ follow by substitution. Since $a^{-1}$ is a unit, $H$ is exactly the submodule of vectors with zero $b_0$-coordinate, so $(q_b)_{b\ne b_0}$ is a basis of $H$ by uniqueness of the expansions in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For $i=2,\ldots,n$ put $c_i=\lambda(v(e_i))$ and define $w:A^{n-1}\to H$ by $w(e_i)=\pi(v(e_i))$. If $w((x_i)_{i=2}^n)=0$, then $v(\sum_{i=2}^nx_ie_i-(\sum_{i=2}^nc_ix_i)e_1)=0$. Injectivity of $v$ and comparison of source coordinates give every $x_i=0$. Thus $w$ is injective with a free target, exactly the case covered by the induction hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05GP, lemma-P-universally-injective, the right vertical arrow in the split-row diagram; explicit free complement and kernel calculation in the local case

proof.text: By the induction hypothesis choose $s:H\to A^{n-1}$ with $sw=1$. For $x\in F$ write $z=s(\pi(x))$ and define $r_v(x)=(\lambda(x)-\sum_{i=2}^nc_iz_i,z_2,\ldots,z_n)$. This is $A$-linear. On $v(e_1)$ one has $\pi(v(e_1))=0$ and $\lambda(v(e_1))=1$, so $r_vv(e_1)=e_1$. On $v(e_i)$ for $i\ge2$ one has $s\pi v(e_i)=e_i$ and $\lambda v(e_i)=c_i$, so $r_vv(e_i)=e_i$. Equality on the basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] proves $r_vv=1$. This completes the induction, including its base case, for all free targets, without any restriction on their ranks.

source.place: Tag 05GP, lemma-P-universally-injective, conclusion from the split-row diagram; explicit retraction in the local free-target case

proof.text: Fix any $A$-module $T$ and $z\in T\otimes_AP$ with $(1_T\otimes u)(z)=0$. The generating and bilinearity properties of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] express $z$ as a finite sum $\sum_{k=1}^dt_k\otimes p_k$. Each $p_k$ has finite basis support by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; let $E\subset I$ be their finite union. Let $j_E:A^E\to P$ take coordinate vectors to the corresponding basis vectors, write $p_k=j_E(\widetilde p_k)$, and set $z_E=\sum_kt_k\otimes\widetilde p_k$. Then $z=(1_T\otimes j_E)(z_E)$. The composite $v=u j_E:A^E\to Q$ is injective, so the completed induction gives $r_E:Q\to A^E$ with $r_Ev=1$. By tensor functoriality, $(1_T\otimes r_E)(1_T\otimes v)=1_{T\otimes_AA^E}$. Since $(1_T\otimes v)(z_E)=(1_T\otimes u)(z)=0$, it follows that $z_E=0$ and therefore $z=0$. The tensor functoriality here is the identity on generators $t\otimes x\mapsto t\otimes r_Ev(x)$, so it holds on the whole tensor product. This proves injectivity for every $T$.

source.place: Tag 05GP, lemma-P-universally-injective, directed finite-free-source reduction; written elementwise using finite basis support instead of invoking a colimit theorem

proof.text: Take $T=A/\mathfrak m$ in the preceding conclusion. The maps interchanging tensor factors, $x\otimes t\mapsto t\otimes x$, are inverse $A$-linear isomorphisms: they are defined by the bilinear universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and their composites are the identity on generators. On generators they identify $u\otimes1_{A/\mathfrak m}$ with $1_{A/\mathfrak m}\otimes u$. Thus the stated right-tensor residue-field map is injective as well.

source.place: Tag 05GP, lemma-P-universally-injective, universal injectivity specialized to the module A/m
